question: Which part had the biggest machine-time saving versus the manual-style program, and by how many minutes?
answer:
**SM-103 had the biggest saving: 28:25 (about 28.4 minutes) less machine time per part.** The manual-style program ran 32:17 (1,937 s) and the best strategy ran 3:52 (232 s), which is 88% less.

SM-103 isn't a real customer part, though. Its data source is `variant_part`, meaning a real CAM run on a part derived from SM-101 for the demo. Among real runs, SM-101 saved the most: 19:21 (1,161 s), going from 22:28 (1,348 s) to 3:07 (187 s), or 86% less. Two other real SM-101 runs saved less, 13:15 (795 s, from 1,183 s to 388 s).

The runner-up overall was SM-106, also a demo variant, which saved 27:17 (1,637 s), from 1,855 s to 218 s. NIST FTC-10 and SM-105 have no baseline or best cycle time recorded, so they aren't in this comparison.
